chapter: Taking New Orleans musicians on the road
title: Local house pianists before they carried their own band
summary: Allen asks about bands in the early days. Mary names Eddie Heywood playing for them in Atlanta, Lovie Austin's father in Chattanooga and Amanda Randolph; each town supplied its own pianist, and they carried a band only from about 1918.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I'm wondering back in those days, what kind of music or band did you carry, any band with you? Any of the New Orleans musicians that early, or when did they start going out with you?
Eddie Haywood used to play. Oh, Eddie Haywood. Eddie Haywood used to play for us in Atlanta, and Professor Lovey Austin's father was playing where? Chattanooga.
Chattanooga, and Mandy that works on the television now. Mandy. Oh, yes. Who is she working with? Father Knows Best?
She worked with lots of different shows, Emerson, Andy, and different ones.
Well, Mandy, she was the mama. Well, now, she played piano in Annapolis. Oh, they had good piano players everywhere.
So, whoever in each city used their own musicians.
Yes, yes, yes. You didn't carry your own... No, not until we...
Well, 1914 was when we took out this... But now that it's time...
